title: Matched introspection admission lane comparison
purpose: Compare the per-process concurrency for shared global introspection budget updates while holding shared quota enforcement, server build, database pool, client population and paced workload constant.

control.arrivalProfile: arrival-baseline: 10-second phases at 200/s, 800/s, 1600/s, and 1200/s noisy invalid-client traffic; then permission-reduction and revocation checks.

environment.topology: One host release Rust process, Node TLS proxy and load generator; Docker Percona primary plus separate Redis cache/limiter containers on loopback. Chromium provisions real login/SSO credentials.

interpretation: Both lane counts preserved the same shared admission checks and recorded zero authority violations, HTTP errors or transport errors in every phase. Two lanes reduced explicit unavailable outcomes in the noisy invalid-client mixture and delivered more authorized resource checks there. One lane delivered more authorized checks in each sustained diverse 800/s and 1600/s run; 200/s results were close. Two runs per setting do not establish a stable winner. The existing two-lane default retains better tolerance in the hostile mixture, while production tuning requires workload-specific evidence.
limitations: Two repetitions per setting on one Apple M5 host, one Rust server process and an owner-role PostgreSQL profile.
Not a multi-process, multi-host, restricted-database-role, production arrival-distribution, endurance or SLO qualification.
Redis and PostgreSQL counters are whole-run snapshots that include setup/probes and are not per-request costs.
Resource deltas are affected by the admitted/rejected outcome mix; they should not be interpreted as isolated lane overhead.
The test applies permission reduction and revocation and checks post-commit behavior, but short local runs do not establish production availability.
